body:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md

>  14.3.2 Verify that web or application server and application framework debug modes are disabled in production to eliminate debug features, developer consoles, and unintended security disclosures.

I think "security disclosures" is not really a thing. I get what is meant by this, but I don't think this is proper English.

comments.body: “Security disclosures” is like a security oracle, revealing info that weakens security - like an error code that reveals the encryption type or similar.

How about:

"14.3.2 Ensure that debug modes for both the web/application server and the application framework are disabled in production environments to prevent exposure of debug features, developer consoles, and unintended sensitive information leakage."

Is that better?

One more version:
Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features, developer consoles, and unintended information leakage.

> One more version: Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features, developer consoles, and unintended information leakage.

I like this. @jmanico @Sjord what do you think?

actually, what is "developer console"? how it's different from "debug feature"? So maybe we can just skip it.

Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features and unintended information leakage.

As the issue was mainly against phrase "security disclosure", I reopen it for category title:
V14.3 Unintended Security Disclosure

Proposal to change it to:
V14.3 Unintended Information Leakage
